Apple has waited an extraordinarily long time to launch its first foldable iPhone, while Samsung's Galaxy Z Fold series has already evolved to its eighth generation.

Apple originally had every reason to wait, but judging by Samsung's recent experience, the iPhone maker's timing could not be more perfect...

Apple's Long Wait

Samsung is one of the most enthusiastic manufacturers developing foldable smartphones, but it quickly discovered that the Korean company had moved too hastily. The first-generation Samsung Galaxy Fold had an extremely fragile screen, and the company ultimately had to withdraw it from the market.

Meanwhile, Apple has been patiently waiting for display technology to mature, with the goal of not only being more durable but also having no visible crease when the device is unfolded. Reports indicate that Apple had to send its own design engineers to help Samsung achieve this goal.

Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Proves the Timing Is Right

As we mentioned last month, the display used in the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 is likely to be very similar to the one that will be used in the upcoming iPhone Ultra. Our sister site 9to5Google found that the Z Fold 8 fully delivered on its promise — the crease in the centre of the screen is barely visible when unfolded.

However, Samsung finally mastering mature display technology is not the only point; consumer demand has also finally caught up. 9to5Google reports that initial demand for the Fold 8 is three times that of the previous generation.

This builds on last year's fifty percent growth in demand.

Of course, these two facts are likely interrelated — a creaseless screen greatly boosts appeal — but given last year's growth, it also shows that foldable phones have been on the market long enough for more people to appreciate the advantages of this form factor.

The iPhone Ultra is expected to debut alongside the iPhone 18 Pro series next month, and the device is anticipated to quickly capture around 25% of the entire foldable smartphone market.
